sections.h2: One project instead of two decisions
body: Most interior repaints stall at the same point: picking colors. Weeks go by with swatches taped to the wall, the start date slides, and in the end someone picks a color under pressure because the crew is coming Monday. Our interior painting with color consultation package takes that step off your plate. The palette is planned, tested, and approved first; then the paint is ordered and the same crew paints the house.

This is different from our standalone color consultation, which is a single session you can book for any project. The bundle is built for whole-home or whole-floor interior repaints, where many rooms have to work together and the color plan and painting schedule need to line up.

sections.h2: Planning the whole floor as one system
body: In an open floor plan, you can see four or five rooms from the front door. If each one was picked separately over the years, the house looks patched together, even when every color is nice on its own. We plan the floor as one system.
bullets: One main wall color that carries through connected living spaces
A single trim and door white used throughout the house
A ceiling color chosen to work with both the walls and the light
One or two accent colors for rooms that can carry them, like a dining room or office
Separate, calmer choices for bedrooms and bathrooms off the main space

body: If there is one thing that makes a repaint look professionally designed, it is one consistent trim color throughout the house. Many Florida homes have three or four slightly different whites on baseboards and doors from years of touch-ups. Pulling them all to the same white, in the same enamel sheen, ties the rooms together instantly. Our trim and molding painting page explains how we prep and finish baseboards, casings, and crown.

sections.h2: A sheen plan for every room
body: Color is only half the decision. The bundle includes a room-by-room sheen plan so each surface gets a finish that suits how it is used: washable satin in kitchens, baths, and hallways; matte or eggshell in living rooms with large windows, where a shinier finish would show every flaw in the drywall; and a harder enamel on trim and doors. Our post on picking a paint finish for any room goes into more detail.
The final plan is written down room by room: wall color, ceiling color, trim color, and sheen for each. You approve it before anything is ordered, and you keep it for future touch-ups.

The package works best for a few kinds of projects. New owners who want the whole interior done before they move in, and want it done once. Families who have lived with builder-grade beige for years and want a real plan. Homeowners who just replaced floors or counters and need walls that work with the new finishes. And empty nesters turning kids' rooms into an office or guest suite, who want those rooms to feel like part of the house rather than leftovers.

If you only need one or two rooms freshened in a color you already know, our regular interior service is the simpler fit. If you are undecided, the walkthrough is free and we can tell you which approach makes more sense for your house.

It starts with the same free walkthrough as any interior job. We measure, note repairs, and talk through how you use each room and what finishes are staying. Then we build a draft palette and bring full-size drawdowns so you can see each color on your own walls in morning and evening light. Once you sign off, the paint is ordered and the job is scheduled.

The painting follows our standard interior painting process: furniture protected, drywall patched and sanded, two finish coats, and room-by-room work so you can stay home. A whole-home interior usually takes three days to two weeks. Because the palette is settled before the crew arrives, there are no mid-project color changes holding things up. If a room needs a third coat because we are covering a deep color with a light one, that is planned into the schedule from the start.
For palette ideas that suit our light, read Florida interior paint colors that work. Homeowners in the area can find local details on our Gainesville interior painting page.

faqs.q: How do I choose colors for a whole house at once?
faqs.a: Start with the finishes that are not changing, such as floors, counters, and cabinets. Pick one main wall color for connected spaces, one trim white for the whole house, and a few accents. Then test large samples in your own light before ordering.

faqs.q: Should all the trim in my house be the same white?
faqs.a: In most homes, yes. One trim and door white in the same sheen throughout is the simplest way to make a repaint look cohesive.

faqs.q: What is included when color consultation is bundled with painting?
faqs.a: A whole-home or whole-floor palette, a room-by-room sheen plan, full-size drawdowns tested on your walls, a written color schedule, and the painting itself by one crew on one schedule.

faqs.q: Can I still change a color after the plan is approved?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is easiest before paint is ordered. Any change after approval is handled in writing so the schedule and estimate stay clear.
